AI coding agent spawns reverse shell referencing cloud/AI secret env vars AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the payoff stage of the 0DIN poisoned-repo / malicious-skill chain: a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw) spawns a shell or netcat that either carries reverse-shell primitives or reads the exact secrets 0DIN flagged as targets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN). This is the credential-theft/backdoor outcome the SkillCloak article warns runs with the agent's own access. Rationale: Combines the article's core warning (a bad skill runs with the agent's access to steal credentials/install a backdoor) with the exact secret names 0DIN enumerated as targets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN) plus canonical reverse-shell primitives. Coding agent parent + shell child + secret/reverse-shell intent is a high-fidelity three-part combination, not bare shell noise. Cross-checked against: • https://aiweekly.co/alerts/0din-clean-github-repos-can-trick-ai-agents-into-reverse-shells • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-skillcloak-technique-lets-malicious.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/new-claude-code-attack/
ATT&CKT1552 T1059.004 T1571
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate skill/setup scripts that echo or export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GITHUB_TOKEN for authenticated operations
  • Developer debugging shells printing environment for troubleshooting
  • CI-style tasks the agent runs that pass GITHUB_TOKEN to gh/git over HTTPS (not a socket)
  • Admins using nc/ncat for benign connectivity tests from a terminal the agent launched
  • PowerShell modules that instantiate Net.Sockets.TCPClient for legitimate service checks
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GITHUB_TOKEN") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("https://","git ","gh ") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("/dev/tcp/","Net.Sockets.TCPClient","socket.socket","-e /bin/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the full command line and the remote endpoint/port — distinguish a secret being passed to a legitimate HTTPS git/gh call from a raw socket or /dev/tcp reverse shell; confirm the parent coding agent and the originating repo/skill. 2) Contain: kill the shell + agent, isolate the host, and immediately rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and AWS keys exposed in that session. 3) Hunt: correlate with the DNS-TXT fetch and .git/ detonation sibling UCs on the same host, enumerate other installed agent skills, and search egress logs for the reverse-shell destination across the fleet.

      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\nc.exe'
      - '\ncat.exe'
  selection_intent:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'
      - 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'
      - 'GITHUB_TOKEN'
      - '/dev/tcp/'
      - '-e /bin/sh'
      - '-e /bin/bash'
      - 'bash -i'
      - 'Net.Sockets.TCPClient'
      - 'socket.socket'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_intent
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\claude.exe OR *\codex.exe OR *\openclaw.exe) @Image:(*\bash.exe OR *\sh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\nc.exe OR *\ncat.exe) @CommandLine:(*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY* OR *AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY* OR *GITHUB_TOKEN* OR */dev/tcp/* OR *bash\ -i* OR *Net.Sockets.TCPClient* OR *socket.socket*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(node|claude|python|python3|codex|openclaw)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|cmd|powershell|pwsh|nc|ncat)\.exe$/i
| regex("(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|GITHUB_TOKEN|/dev/tcp/|-e /bin/(sh|bash)|bash -i|Net\\.Sockets\\.TCPClient|socket\\.socket)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY*" OR Processes.process="*AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY*" OR Processes.process="*GITHUB_TOKEN*" OR Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*-e /bin/sh*" OR Processes.process="*-e /bin/bash*" OR Processes.process="*bash -i*" OR Processes.process="*Net.Sockets.TCPClient*" OR Processes.process="*socket.socket*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","claude.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","codex.exe","openclaw.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY*" OR Processes.process="*AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY*" OR Processes.process="*GITHUB_TOKEN*" OR Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*-e /bin/sh*" OR Processes.process="*-e /bin/bash*" OR Processes.process="*bash -i*" OR Processes.process="*Net.Sockets.TCPClient*" OR Processes.process="*socket.socket*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("91.92.242.30", "2.26.75.16") or RemoteUrl has_any ("laosji.net", "letssendit.fun", "download.setup-service.com", "install.app-distribution.net", "openclawcli.vercel.app")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["91.92.242.30", "2.26.75.16"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["laosji.net", "letssendit.fun", "download.setup-service.com", "install.app-distribution.net", "openclawcli.vercel.app"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or SHA1 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or MD5 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or SHA1 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7") or MD5 in~ ("818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["818aea6143282b352fdfdc0f3ebf77a36e54eb3befb5cad1a355a99ab97c6aa7", "b6c7e0bf573b1c7d9d3a05eb08d26579199515b847df984862805f44a7af8007", "b30eaed1f7478c28f4ec50d07ed5ef014ffbc4b2bc5a38d689ba9f7abb5e19c2", "ebb73dbb5aac1f6fe1a88e8f26126a1e1aa34c9f3345ad4345189b40d9bf1d1d", "f4e41aa269c88bf11a2022701a9cf41e9a186aa1b224d837c31bf34e0b875d0e", "881ce5cb124c4d2e814783724cc1388f6a1cbf6eee274c3f3366e77ba3503ad7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Langflow CVE-2025-3248 exploitation via /api/v1/validate/code (JadePuffer initial access) · [LLM] Nacos CVE-2021-29441 auth bypass — rogue admin creation via Nacos-Server User-Agent
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JadePuffer C2 beacon to attacker infrastructure (45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] JadePuffer MySQL/Nacos database extortion — AES_ENCRYPT + README_RANSOM table · [LLM] Langflow web-service account spawning DB dump / MinIO enumeration (post-RCE recon) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Langflow CVE-2025-3248 exploitation via /api/v1/validate/code (JadePuffer initial access) AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated POST requests to the Langflow code-validation endpoint that JadePuffer abused for RCE (CVE-2025-3248) to gain its foothold. Article-specific because it targets the exact vulnerable path and HTTP verb rather than generic web exploitation. Rationale: Uses the exact vulnerable path (/api/v1/validate/code) and POST verb from CVE-2025-3248, confirmed by Zscaler ThreatLabz and the Langflow GHSA. Defender AH has no web-application-layer table so defender_kql is intentionally empty; the endpoint-side outcome is covered by the Langflow post-exploit recon UC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/cve-2025-3248-rce-vulnerability-langflow • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-3248 • https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-vwmf-pq79-vjvx • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authenticated Langflow developers validating flow code on patched 1.3.0+ instances
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Nuclei) probing the endpoint as part of authorized scans
  • Internal CI/CD pipelines that call the validate endpoint
  • Security team replaying the PoC during a controlled test
  • Langflow health-check tooling POSTing benign snippets
Suppression filter
| where HttpStatusCode !in ("401","403") and DstHostname !in~ ("langflow-dev.internal","langflow-staging.internal")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP and HTTP status for the POST to /api/v1/validate/code; a 200 on an internet-facing, pre-1.3.0 Langflow host = likely successful RCE. Check the request body for decorator/default-arg payloads calling exec(). 2) Contain: isolate the Langflow host, rotate any cloud credentials/API keys and DB passwords stored in its environment, and confirm Langflow is on 1.3.0+. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for python/uvicorn spawning shells, pg_dump of the Langflow PostgreSQL DB, MinIO enumeration, and a new cron beacon (see companion UCs).
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v1/validate/code"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nacos CVE-2021-29441 auth bypass — rogue admin creation via Nacos-Server User-Agent AIExploitation High
Detects the Nacos authentication-bypass JadePuffer used to create rogue administrator accounts, keyed on the spoofed 'Nacos-Server' User-Agent hitting the /nacos/v1/auth/users management endpoint. High fidelity because that UA on the user-management path from a non-cluster source is the exact CVE-2021-29441 backdoor signature. Rationale: Combines the CVE-2021-29441 backdoor signature (User-Agent: Nacos-Server, confirmed by Tenable/NVD/GHSA) with the specific /nacos/v1/auth/users account-creation path the article cites for rogue-admin creation. Requests from outside the Nacos cluster peer set carrying this UA are almost always exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/plugins/nessus/154416 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-29441 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-36hp-jr8h-556f • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion
ATT&CKT1190 T1136.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-node Nacos cluster peers syncing config (send Nacos-Server UA between known cluster IPs)
  • Security scanners with a CVE-2021-29441 signature/Nuclei template
  • Nacos health probes replaying cluster requests
  • Migration tooling bulk-creating service accounts via the auth API
  • Load balancers preserving the upstream Nacos UA
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.0.0.0/8_nacos_peers") // replace with your Nacos cluster peer IP set; keep external and non-peer internal sources
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP is NOT a member of the legitimate Nacos cluster peer set; a POST/PUT to /nacos/v1/auth/users with a 200 from an external IP = rogue admin created. 2) Contain: disable/delete any Nacos accounts created in the window, force-rotate Nacos admin and MySQL root credentials, and patch Nacos to >=1.4.1. 3) Hunt: pivot to the backing MySQL server for AES_ENCRYPT of config_info, dropped config_info/history tables, and a README_RANSOM table (companion impact UC).
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "/nacos/v1/auth/users"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has "Nacos-Server"
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

JadePuffer C2 beacon to attacker infrastructure (45.131.66.106 / 64.20.53.230) AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on outbound connections to the two JadePuffer C2 IPs used by the cron beacon installed on the compromised Langflow host (~every 30 minutes). Direct IOC match on the campaign's command-and-control infrastructure. Rationale: Direct match on the two C2 IPs tied to the 30-minute cron beacon. Confidence held at Medium because the IPs are single-sourced to Sysdig's report (no independent second-source confirmation found); the campaign, TTPs and both CVEs are corroborated across 6+ outlets. Validate IP freshness before alerting long-term. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ai-agent-exploits-langflow-rce-to.html • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/07/02/smooth-ai-criminal-drives-first-end-to-end-agentic-ransomware-attack/5266073
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1053.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosting IP later reassigned to a legitimate service (VPS churn)
  • Threat-intel/sandbox detonation infrastructure deliberately touching the IOC
  • Security researcher validation traffic from a jump box
  • Proxy/NAT egress aggregating many hosts behind one src IP, obscuring the real beacon origin
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process on the source host — a beacon from cron/curl/wget on an internet-facing Langflow or Nacos box is high-severity. Confirm periodicity (~30 min). 2) Contain: block both IPs at the egress firewall, isolate the host, and remove the malicious cron entry (check /etc/cron*, /var/spool/cron, and per-user crontabs). 3) Hunt: enumerate every host that contacted these IPs, then look for the Langflow RCE, Nacos auth bypass, and MySQL ransomware artifacts across those hosts.
DeviceNetworkEvents

| where RemoteIP in ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("45.131.66.106","64.20.53.230")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

JadePuffer MySQL/Nacos database extortion — AES_ENCRYPT + README_RANSOM table AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the destructive impact stage where JadePuffer encrypted 1,342 Nacos config_info items with MySQL AES_ENCRYPT(), dropped the config_info/history tables, and created a README_RANSOM extortion table. Keys on the highly specific README_RANSOM table name and the AES_ENCRYPT-over-config_info pattern. Rationale: README_RANSOM is the exact extortion table name Sysdig captured, and AES_ENCRYPT-over-config_info is the precise MySQL encryption pattern against Nacos's config table — both are near-unique to this operation. Splunk/Defender/Falcon/auditd pivot on the mysql CLI command line; Sentinel pivots on the MySQL server log (SyslogMessage) since DB query logs are the natural Sentinel telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ai-agent-exploits-langflow-rce-to.html • https://www.scworld.com/news/1st-agentic-ransomware-jadepuffer-invades-database-at-machine-speed
ATT&CKT1486 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A DBA legitimately running AES_ENCRYPT against an application table coincidentally named config_info
  • Backup/migration scripts that reference README_RANSOM after a real incident (for cleanup)
  • Detection engineers replaying the SQL PoC in a lab
  • Application-level encryption feature that column-encrypts Nacos config values
  • DB integration tests seeding a table named README_RANSOM
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "restore" and AccountName !in~ ("dba_backup","svc_migration")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the statements ran against the production Nacos MySQL instance and whether config_info/his_config_info were dropped and README_RANSOM created; capture the executing DB user and source host. 2) Contain: take the DB offline, snapshot for forensics, restore config_info from the last known-good backup, and rotate MySQL root plus any Nacos-stored secrets. Note the AES key is never persisted by JadePuffer — do not expect to recover data via the attacker. 3) Hunt: trace back to the Langflow foothold and Nacos auth-bypass (companion UCs), and confirm no other databases received AES_ENCRYPT/DROP payloads.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "README_RANSOM"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "AES_ENCRYPT" and ProcessCommandLine has "config_info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("mysqld","mysql")
| where SyslogMessage has "README_RANSOM"
   or (SyslogMessage has "AES_ENCRYPT" and SyslogMessage has "config_info")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: JadePuffer Nacos Database Extortion via MySQL AES_ENCRYPT and README_RANSOM

Langflow web-service account spawning DB dump / MinIO enumeration (post-RCE recon) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the JadePuffer post-exploitation recon on the Langflow host: the Langflow Python/uvicorn service spawning pg_dump/psql (dumping Langflow's PostgreSQL DB) or curl/wget/mc reaching a MinIO object store (:9000). Article-specific parent→child chain that a web app should never legitimately produce. Rationale: Ties the article's post-RCE actions (dumped Langflow PostgreSQL, enumerated MinIO object store) to a concrete parent→child process chain: the Langflow python/uvicorn service should never legitimately launch pg_dump or reach a MinIO API. Kept hunting/Medium because backup jobs can invoke pg_dump; the MinIO/:9000 branch is the higher-fidelity half. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ai-agent-exploits-langflow-rce-to.html
ATT&CKT1005 T1530 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled Langflow backup job invoking pg_dump under the same service account
  • Legitimate app code shelling out to curl for a MinIO/S3 health check on :9000
  • Container init scripts running psql migrations at startup
  • Ops engineer manually dumping the Langflow DB from within the app container
  • APM/monitoring agents probing the MinIO endpoint
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cron","backup","/etc/cron") and FileName in~ ("pg_dump","psql"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child command line — an interactive pg_dump of the Langflow DB or ad-hoc curl to a MinIO :9000 endpoint from the web-service account (not a scheduled backup) is suspicious; correlate timing with the /api/v1/validate/code exploit UC. 2) Contain: isolate the host, rotate PostgreSQL/MinIO and any environment-stored cloud credentials, and review MinIO access logs for bucket enumeration/downloads. 3) Hunt: check for the follow-on cron C2 beacon and the pivot to the Nacos MySQL server (companion UCs).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where (FileName in~ ("pg_dump","psql"))
   or (FileName in~ ("curl","wget","mc") and (ProcessCommandLine has ":9000" or ProcessCommandLine has "minio"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("pg_dump","psql"))
   or (TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","mc") and (TargetProcessCommandLine has ":9000" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "minio"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
